requirements.quote: With `merge_train: off`, lanes and batches behave exactly as before.
With `merge_train: on`, a lane with pending checks ends `pr-ready` and its slot admits the next issue at once.
The train merges green PRs one at a time per base, with `--match-head-commit` set to the reviewed head, then closes the issue, sets `workflow:merged` and deletes the branch.
Red hands the PR back as `ci.red`, naming the failing checks and their URLs, and a recovery lane runs.
Conflict hands it back as `base.conflict`.
Dependents wait for the train's merge.
A stopped batch reports `pr-ready` rows, and `--resume` continues them.
The batch report has a `merge train:` line: merged, handed back by code, train wait p50, base-syncs.
When the train is on, a lane whose reviewed PR has pending required checks ends with a new terminal reason, `pr-ready` (code `awaiting_merge`).
It returns `{pr, head, required, policy, lane}` and the batch runner frees its slot.
A red check still gets the lane's own CI fix round.
A lane whose checks are already green merges itself.
Only a plain merge is handed over. A split, an e2e gate, numbered sequence files or close-time records keep the lane waiting.
`bin/lean/mergetrain.mjs` adds a minimal serial train in the batch runner (`orchestrate.mjs`). Its state is persisted in the batch `state.json` as `train`.
Each poll it merges at most one green PR per lane base at the reviewed head.
A green PR that is behind its base gets `gh pr update-branch`.
Red, conflicting or moved-head PRs are handed back as `needs-human` `ci.red` / `base.conflict` / `merge.head_mismatch`. In-batch recovery then requeues a fix lane.
No batching and no bisection.
Scope (phase 1, behind `orchestration.merge_train: off|on`, default off)
behind `orchestration.merge_train: off|on`, default off
requirements.why: Default-off flag. First cohort: one low-traffic repo lane base. Guard metrics: lifecycle minutes p50, needs-human rate, ci.red/merge.head_mismatch hand-backs, train wait p50. Shadow evidence: batch reports with the `merge train:` line from a cohort run.

deliverables.change: New module: createTrain({gh, state, now}) with persisted train state, tick() merging at most one green PR per base via `gh pr merge --merge --match-head-commit <head>`, `gh pr update-branch` when behind, hand-back (ci.red with failing check names+URLs, base.conflict, merge.head_mismatch), shared post-merge close sequence call, wait p50 and base-sync stats, summary line formatter. No batching, no bisection.
Unit tests on injected gh: serial per base, match-head-commit, update-branch when behind, red/conflict/head-mismatch hand-back, state persistence and resume, p50, report line.

Add `mergeTrain` option (default off). In step 7 CI wait, when on, checks pending, and plain merge (no split, e2e gate, sequence lease, close-time records) finish('pr-ready') with {pr, head, required, policy, lane}; red keeps the CI fix round; green merges in-lane. Extract the post-merge close/label/branch-delete steps into a helper reused by the train. Off path unchanged.
Tests: off unchanged; on+pending gives pr-ready with payload; on+green self-merges; red fix round; split/e2e/sequence/close-time records keep waiting.

Wire the train: tick during polling, pr-ready rows free the slot, dependents wait until train merge (SATISFIED handling), train state in state.json, resume of pr-ready rows, hand-back rows enter in-batch recovery, `merge train:` report line. Off path unchanged.
New orchestrate tests: slot frees at pr-ready, dependents wait, stopped batch reports pr-ready and resume continues, hand-back requeues recovery, report line, off unchanged.
Add `train` to state.json shape and make `pr-ready` resumable/requeuable (REQUEUABLE at :113).
Map `pr-ready` to AWAITING_MERGE; add ci.red code if missing; treat pr-ready alongside ci-pending in recovery classification.
Test that merge_train accepts off|on, rejects others, defaults off.
Document pr-ready terminal, mergeTrain option, shared post-merge helper.
Document the merge train, state.json `train`, report line, flag default off.

decisions.choice: Reuse the lane's post-merge close sequence via an extracted helper instead of copying it into the train.
decisions.justification: Issue requires reuse; the sequence sits after the lane merge at bin/lean/lean.mjs:4233.

decisions.choice: New orchestrate tests go in a new file orchestrate-train.test.mjs, following the orchestrate-*.test.mjs per-feature convention.
